arxiv-2106-08696.title: High-Quality Hypergraph Partitioning DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Journal: JEA Volume: 42 42 42 12 CCS: Mathematics of computing Hypergraphs CCS: Theory of computation Graph algorithms analysis CCS: Theory of computation Dynamic graph algorithms
arxiv-2106-08696.creator: Sebastian Schlag, Tobias Heuer, Lars Gottesbüren, Yaroslav Akhremtsev, Christian Schulz, Peter Sanders
arxiv-2106-08696.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Schlag, Tobias Heuer, Lars Gottesbüren, Yaroslav Akhremtsev, Christian Schulz, Peter Sanders. Hypergraphs are a generalization of graphs where edges (aka nets ) are allowed to connect more than two vertices. They have a similarly wide range of applications as graphs. This paper considers the fundamental and intensively studied problem of balanced hypergraph partitioning , which asks for partitioning the vertices into k k disjoint blocks of bounded size while minimizing an objective function over the hyperedges.

arxiv-2110-07964.title: Federated Route Leak Detection in Inter-domain Routing with Privacy Guarantee
arxiv-2110-07964.creator: Man Zeng, Dandan Li, Pei Zhang, Kun Xie, Xiaohong Huang
arxiv-2110-07964.description: Abstract In the inter-domain network, a route leak occurs when a routing announcement is propagated outside of its intended scope, which is a violation of the agreed routing policy. The route leaks can disrupt the internet traffic and cause large outages. The accurately detection of route leaks requires the share of AS business relationship information of ASes.

arxiv-2112-01182.title: Age of Information in Prioritized Random Access This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No 101022113.
arxiv-2112-01182.creator: Khac-Hoang Ngo, Giuseppe Durisi, and Alexandre Graell i Amat
arxiv-2112-01182.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Khac-Hoang Ngo, Giuseppe Durisi, and Alexandre Graell i Amat. Age of information (AoI) is a performance metric that captures the freshness of status updates. While AoI has been studied thoroughly for point-to-point links, the impact of modern random-access protocols on this metric is still unclear. In this paper, we extend the recent results by Munari to prioritized random access where devices are divided into different classes according to different AoI requirements.

arxiv-2203-06199.title: The faint light in groups and clusters of galaxies
arxiv-2203-06199.creator: Mireia Montes
arxiv-2203-06199.description: Abstract The diffuse light that spreads through groups and clusters of galaxies is made of free-floating stars not bound to any galaxy. This is known as the intracluster light (ICL) and holds important clues for understanding the evolution of these large structures.

arxiv-2204-10968.title: Cooperative colorings of forests
arxiv-2204-10968.creator: Peter Bradshaw
arxiv-2204-10968.description: Abstract . Given a family 𝒢 \mathcal{G} of graphs spanning a common vertex set V V , a cooperative coloring of 𝒢 \mathcal{G} is a collection of one independent set from each graph G ∈ 𝒢 G\in\mathcal{G} such that the union of these independent sets equals V V .

arxiv-2406-16382.description: Abstract Sequential decision-making refers to algorithms that take into account the dynamics of the environment, where early decisions affect subsequent decisions. With large language models (LLMs) demonstrating powerful capability between tasks, we can’t help but ask: Can Current LLMs Effectively Make Sequential Decisions?

arxiv-2506-11834.title: Magnon-plasmon hybridization mediated by Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in two-dimensional crystals: tuning with electric field
arxiv-2506-11834.creator: Wojciech Rudziński 1, Mirali Jafari 1, Józef Barnaś 2, Anna Dyrdał 1
arxiv-2506-11834.description: Abstract Recently, a mechanism of magnon-plasmon hybridization in ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic systems, based on spin-orbit interaction associated with mobile (conduction) electrons has been proposed. Here, we consider another mechanism of magnon-plasmon hybridization, which is based on spin-orbit coupling attributed to localized spins and leading to the antisymmetric exchange (Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya) interaction.

arxiv-2510-06109.title: Phase-induced switching of ferromagnetic insulators in Josephson spin valves
arxiv-2510-06109.creator: A. A. Mazanik, C.-H. Huang, Miguel A. Cazalilla, F. S. Bergeret
arxiv-2510-06109.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A. A. Mazanik, C.-H. Huang, Miguel A. Cazalilla, F. S. Bergeret. We study the Josephson effect in junctions composed of two ferromagnetic insulator/diffusive superconductor bilayers separated by an insulating barrier. By computing the free energy of the system, we identify two distinct contributions: (i) The work performed by a current source to create a supercurrent through the junction, and (ii) an antiferromagnetic coupling between ferromagnetic insulators, mediated by the superconducting condensate across the insulating barrier.

arxiv-2511-07873.title: Schottky Anomaly of five-Dimensional de Sitter Hairy Spacetime based on effective thermodynamic quantities

arxiv-2511-07873.description: Abstract Taking the mass, charge, hair parameter, and cosmological constant of the 5-dimensional de Sitter hairy spacetime as the state variables of a thermodynamic system, and based on the satisfaction of the universal first law of thermodynamics, we obtain the effective thermodynamic quantities of the spacetime.

pmc-11714809.title: An automated method for quantifying syntactic complexity of spontaneous speech in Primary Progressive Aphasia
pmc-11714809.creator: Galit Agmon, Sunghye Cho, Sharon Ash, Katheryn A Q Cousins, Sameer Pradhan, Yoon Duk Kim, Mark Y Liberman, David J Irwin, Naomi Nevler
pmc-11714809.description: BackgroundReduced syntactic complexity is the predominant linguistic impairment unique to the nonfluent agrammatic variant of PPA (naPPA).Reliable, objective and automatic methods for assessing syntactic complexity are currently lacking. Here, we introduce an automatic method for quantifying syntactic complexity in speech. We show that this method differentiates naPPA from other subtypes and monitors disease progression and severity.

pmc-12640659.description: Marine sponges of the genus Oceanapia are prolific producers of bioactive secondary metabolites.
